discussion_comments.comment_body:
[P1] Keep the fresh-session handoff consistent across harnesses

The shared directive now tells every harness to stop after `intent-birth`, but only Claude’s orchestrator skill was updated. Codex, Kiro, Kiro IDE, and OpenCode still instruct the conductor to re-run `next` in the same session, preserving the stale-context bug this change intends to fix. The shared message also says `/aidlc`, while Codex uses `$aidlc`. Please update every harness-specific skill and tailor the resume command.

**[MAJOR, blocking] Plugin test results collide by basename, so a FAIL can roll up green.**

Result names derive from the file basename only (`const base = basename(file)` in runBunTestFile, and writeMeta writes `_results/<name>.meta`), so two plugins that both ship `plugin.test.ts` write the same `_results/plugin.meta`, last writer wins, and a failing suite is erased from summary.txt/failures.txt whenever the passing one finishes later. The `tests/<level>/` layout could never collide (one directory, unique names); this new multi-directory discovery is what makes it reachable, and the fixture header explicitly tells plugin authors to copy the shape. This is the same result-masking class as the t188 gap we blocked on in round 2, so I would rather not ship it in the same PR that fixed that. Keying the result name by the plugin dir (e.g. `plugin-test-pro`) closes it; same treatment for this line's bare-basename exclude, which today would drop every plugin's suite at once.

Fixed in `54faa29`. Result meta is now keyed by the plugin dir: a test under `plugins/<plugin>/tests/` gets name `plugin-<plugin>-<stem>` (e.g. `plugin-test-pro-plugin`), not the bare basename, so two plugins' `plugin.test.ts` can't overwrite each other's `.meta` — a FAIL can no longer be erased by a later PASS. The plugin-file exclude is keyed the same qualified way (so excluding one plugin's suite doesn't drop all of them). Verified the runner discovers + runs it and the meta name is qualified.

`/aidlc space-create -h` reaches here with `raw = "-h"`, and `slugify("-h")` is `"h"`, which isn't in RESERVED_RECORD_NAMES. So the guard doesn't fire and the space gets created. Same on the Kiro seam path.

An early check before slugify would close it:
```ts
if (raw === "-h" || raw === "help") die("Did you mean /aidlc --help? To create a space, pass a name.");
```
